claims.text: Maternal GBS colonisation status and culture results are unavailable, creating uncertainty about vertical transmission risk for this 32‑week, 6‑hour old neonate.
Because risk factors cannot be excluded, NICE advises offering intrapartum antibiotics to mothers with possible GBS exposure or chorioamnionitis.
Perform an immediate clinical assessment, review maternal and neonatal history, and obtain a full physical examination with vital signs as soon as possible.

If any clinical indicators of possible early‑onset infection appear (e.g., temperature instability, respiratory distress, abnormal labs), escalate to full sepsis work‑up and start empirical antibiotics.
Interpret cerebrospinal fluid results in the context of the clinical picture and maternal history once obtained.
Explain to parents that missing maternal culture data and an incomplete exam increase uncertainty, and that close monitoring and possible treatment are being pursued.

packet.evaluation_question: Maternal history and culture results are unavailable and the latest examination is missing. Explain uncertainty and the assessment needed without assuming normal findings. Gestation 32 weeks; age 6 hours; setting hospital birth.

evidence.text: Offer an immediate birth (by induction of labour or caesarean birth) to women, trans men and non-binary people who are between 34 and 37 weeks' gestation who: • have prolonged prelabour rupture of membranes and • have group B streptococcal colonisation, bacteriuria or infection at any time in their current pregnancy. [2021]

Offer antibiotics during labour to women, trans men and non-binary people who: • are in pre-term labour or • have group B streptococcal colonisation, bacteriuria or infection during the current pregnancy or • have had group B streptococcal colonisation, bacteriuria or infection in a previous pregnancy, and have not had a negative test for group B streptococcus by enrichment culture or polymerase chain reaction (PCR) on a rectovaginal swab samples collected between 35 and 37 weeks' gestation or 3 to 5 weeks before the anticipated delivery date in the current pregnancy or • have had a previous baby with an invasive group B streptococcal infection or • have a clinical diagnosis of chorioamnionitis. [2021]
Interpret cerebrospinal fluid results in babies alongside the clinical presentation and maternal history. [2024]

If there are any risk factors for early-onset neonatal infection (see box 1 on risk- factors for early-onset neonatal infection), or if there are clinical indicators of possible early-onset neonatal infection (see box 2 on clinical indicators of possible early-onset neonatal infection): • perform an immediate clinical assessment • review the maternal and neonatal history • carry out a physical examination of the baby, including an assessment of vital signs. [2021]
